item.title: A Community Land Trust Is Raising the Bar for Community Power in Economic Development
item.description: Denver’s Tierra Colectiva is showing how residents can shape — and own — mixed-use projects at a scale once reserved for private developers.

item.title: This Bronx Project Is Setting a New Standard for Community-Controlled Development
item.description: After decades of failed mega-projects, the Kingsbridge Armory is now the site of one of the country’s most ambitious experiments in community ownership and shared control.

item.title: Residents Halted Development on a Historic Burial Ground. Now They Want a Say in What Comes Next.
item.description: Flatbush residents want a collaborative memorial process. Instead, they say the city is moving ahead with little transparency and even less community input.

item.title: A Century-Old Adobe Schoolhouse Is Being Restored as a Community Hub in New Mexico
item.description: A small town in northern New Mexico is punching above its weight with a local historic preservation project.

item.title: Black Commercial Corridors Are Still Banking On Culture
item.description: From West Oakland to Birmingham, historic commercial districts in Black neighborhoods are using cultural preservation to drive community investment.

item.title: This Spanish City Is Resurrecting a 3,000-Year-Old Solution To Fight Extreme Heat
item.description: Seville is experimenting with underground aqueduct networks to beat the heat, building upon an ancient Middle Eastern urban cooling system.

item.title: The Long Road to Family Reunification
item.description: A Philadelphia mother’s fight to reunite with her children offers a grim window into the problems of the American cities’ child welfare systems – and how they can be improved.

item.title: Oakland Figure Skater Alysa Liu’s Gold Medal Story Has a Surprising Lesson for Cities
item.description: A joyful, ebullient performance on ice provides a reason to look back at a landmark community investment program that no longer exists.

item.title: The Bobafication of Manhattan’s Chinatown
item.description: The proliferation of bubble tea shops displacing Chinatown’s legacy businesses might not “look” like gentrification. That makes it even more insidious, some say.

item.title: Take a Walk Around the Block With Me
item.description: After two decades of neighborhood walks with residents, Gabrielle Bendiner-Viani’s new book, “The Cities We Need,” shows the vital everyday labor between people and places that makes community possible.
